# requireAbsolute

<link-summary>Returns the value as an absolute path, or throws.</link-summary>

<web-summary>requireAbsolute() — Returns the value as an absolute path, or throws. apps-script-utils, English.</web-summary>

<tldr>
<p>Module: <code>net/path</code> · Since: 1.11.0</p>
</tldr>

```typescript
function requireAbsolute(path: unknown, message: string = "Expected an absolute path."): string;
```

A path that starts at a root: a leading `/`, or a scheme such as `https://` or `mailto:`. Everything else, the empty string included, is relative.

`isX` and `nonX` answer a question and never interrupt control flow; `requireX` and `requireNonX` hand the value back or throw. The scheme is explained in [](validation-conventions.md).

## Parameters

| Parameter                                               | Type      | Description                                                   |
| :------------------------------------------------------ | :-------- | :------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `path`                                                  | `unknown` | The value to validate as an absolute path.                    |
| `message` _(optional)_ `= "Expected an absolute path."` | `string`  | The message of the exception. A default is used when omitted. |

## Returns

`string` — the same value, typed as an absolute path.

## Throws

| Exception                  | Condition                          |
| :------------------------- | :--------------------------------- |
| `IllegalArgumentException` | the value is not an absolute path. |

## Examples

### What passes and what does not

```javascript
requireAbsolute("/var/log"); // => "/var/log"
requireAbsolute("https://example.com/a"); // => "https://example.com/a"
requireAbsolute("docs/readme.md"); // throws IllegalArgumentException
requireAbsolute("./a"); // throws IllegalArgumentException
```
